page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, this server provides 4 vCPUs split across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system features 8.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local NVMe storage and relies on external block storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

The x86_64 architecture incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 KB of L1d cache. Advanced vector and encryption instructions are supported, including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation (avx512f), Vector Neural Network Instructions (avx512_vnni), AES, FMA, and BMI2. Hardware-assisted virtualization is provided through the hypervisor flag.

Performance tests show moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core capacity due to the 2 physical core limit. Benchmark results record a Geekbench single-core score of 1160.0 and a multi-core score of 2539.0. PassMark CPU performance is measured at 4268.04, while stress-ng multi-core testing achieves 3490.35. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 25.0 GB/sec for uncached reads and 21.81 GB/sec for uncached writes. Database throughput yields 3.32 million Redis SET operations per second, with static web serving reaching 3.78 GB/sec.

Without local SSD storage, the instance relies entirely on attached network volumes. The dedicated vCPU architecture guarantees predictable CPU allocation without burst-credit throttling, offering cost-efficient compute capacity for non-memory-bound workloads. Typical operational fits include lightweight web serving, microservices, basic software compilation, and routine batch processing jobs.
